stories.title: KeyBank Expands to 113K SF at Elecor’s 1301 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: A major banking institution has added 15,292 square feet to its Manhattan office footprint, Commercial Observer has learned. Keybank signed a 15-year deal to renew its existing space and expand to 112,924 square feet at Elecor Properties’ 1301 Avenue of the Americas across the entire 35th, 36th and 37th floors, as well as portions of the 28th and 38th floors, according to the landlord. Asking rent for the Plaza District office tower was not disclosed, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown in the second quarter of 2026 was $86.18 per square foot, according to a report from CBRE. “As KeyBank continues to grow and adapt to the evolving needs of our business, we remain focused on providing our employees with an environment that fosters collaboration and connection,” John Manginelli, Hudson Valley and metro New York market president at KeyBank, said in a statement. “Expanding our footprint at 1301 Avenue of the Americas enables us to support that vision while positioning us for continued growth and enhanced service to our clients across the region.” JLL’s Matthew Astrachan, Justin Haber, Kyle Riker, Adam Hill and Bob Beckstedt represented KeyBank in the transaction, while Peter Brindley, Douglas Neye and Sean Kirk handled negotiations in-house for Elecor Properties. “This was a highly strategic transaction that addressed several priorities at once: securing more space for KeyBank’s growing businesses, keeping its teams together within one elevator bank, creating the opportunity to upgrade the existing workplace, and establishing a true New York City headquarters with prominent signage,” Astrachan said in a statement. Other tenants in the building between West 52nd and West 53rd streets include investment bank Piper Sandler, which signed a lease for 140,000 square feet in August 2025, back when Elecor was still Paramount Group. bullets: KeyBank expands to 112,924 SF at 1301 Avenue of the Americas, Manhattan, 15-year renewal.
Midtown office asking rent $86.18/SF in Q2 2026; major tenant commitment signals demand.
Occupies entire 35th, 36th, 37th floors plus portions of 28th, 38th in Plaza District.
stories.summary: KeyBank signed a 15-year lease expanding its Manhattan footprint to 112,924 square feet at Elecor Properties' 1301 Avenue of the Americas in Midtown, adding 15,292 SF to existing space across multiple full and partial floors. The deal reflects continued institutional demand for premium office despite sector headwinds. Midtown office asking rents averaged $86.18/SF in Q2 2026, underscoring the Plaza District's resilience.
stories.impact: Large financial-services tenant commitment to expanded Midtown footprint signals institutional confidence in Manhattan's office market and workplace strategy despite elevated cap rates and financing constraints. This demand supports land and development economics for office-to-residential conversion plays and mixed-use projects in Manhattan's core, though the broader office sector remains in recovery-recession bifurcation.

stories.title: League City Developer Pursuing Nearly 300K-SF of Retail, Industrial Space
stories.excerpt: Alexander Grene Development broke ground on the $78 million mixed-use business park Lilac Field in League City. The development is seeking its first industrial and retail tenants. Located between League City Parkway and SH 146, Lilac Field will span 24.5 acres and include 70,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space and 220,000 square feet of flexible warehouse space. Community Impact reports once complete, Lilac Field will include 16 small warehouse units and seven retail and restaurant buildings, with warehouse tenants expected to include entertainment venues, gyms, childcare providers and breweries. The development’s first two industrial buildings are expected to be completed by early 2027. The developer is seeking industrial clients, such as aerospace and aviation suppliers, marine service groups, technology firms, energy service companies, advanced manufacturing users and specialty distributors to rent its warehouse space. The full buildout is projected to take three to five years. The post League City Developer Pursuing Nearly 300K-SF of Retail, Industrial Space appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Alexander Grene Development breaks ground on $78M Lilac Field mixed-use park in League City, Texas.
290,000 SF total: 220,000 SF flexible warehouse, 70,000 SF retail/restaurant on 24.5 acres.
First two industrial buildings complete early 2027; targets aerospace, marine, tech, advanced manufacturing tenants.
stories.summary: Alexander Grene Development has broken ground on Lilac Field, a $78 million, 24.5-acre mixed-use business park in League City between League City Parkway and SH 146. The development will deliver 220,000 square feet of warehouse, 70,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space, and 16 small warehouse units across seven retail/restaurant buildings. First industrial buildings are expected to complete in early 2027.
stories.impact: Speculative industrial and flex-warehouse development in League City signals strong regional demand for last-mile logistics and advanced manufacturing space tied to Houston's broader industrial and energy-services corridor. The developer's targeting of aerospace, marine, tech, and specialty distributors reflects in-migration of skilled manufacturing and supply-chain diversification away from coastal hubs—a demand catalyst for multifamily in the League City submarket as workforce follows job creation.

stories.title: Prosper Developer Planning $240M Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: Developer Naseem Shaik is moving forward on a $240 million Prosper project that will include a hotel, offices, retail and restaurants. No multifamily is planned at the time. Dubbed Bella Prosper, it will sit on 61 acres with a large manmade lake in the middle. The development will incorporate one-story offices as well as office space above restaurant and retail spaces. Features of Bella Prosper include a 139-key hotel geared toward business travelers, a public parking deck and a park with a water feature. Bella Prosper is slated to build at least 60,950 square feet of retail space. Community Impact reports Bella Prosper is expected to create $59.8 million in annual taxable sales. Developers estimate that Bella Prosper as a whole will generate $88.3 million in net benefits for the town over the next 25 years. Construction on Phase 1 was originally expected to start in late 2027. The post Prosper Developer Planning $240M Mixed-Use Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Naseem Shaik planning $240M Bella Prosper mixed-use project on 61 acres in Prosper, Texas.
Mix: 139-key hotel, office, 60,950 SF retail, restaurants, parking deck; no multifamily currently planned.
Expected to generate $88.3M net benefits over 25 years; Phase 1 construction originally slated late 2027.
stories.summary: Developer Naseem Shaik is advancing a $240 million Bella Prosper project on 61 acres in Prosper, Texas, featuring a 139-key business-traveler hotel, office space (including ground-floor and upper-level configurations), 60,950 square feet of retail, restaurants, public parking, and a waterfront park. The development is projected to generate $59.8 million in annual taxable sales and $88.3 million in net municipal benefits over 25 years. Phase 1 construction was originally scheduled to begin in late 2027.
stories.impact: Absence of multifamily in Bella Prosper despite large-scale development in fast-growing Prosper (north Dallas exurb) suggests either development economics disfavor residential at this site, or pipeline saturation in Prosper already underway. Developers should monitor whether office-and-hotel-anchored projects are cannibalizing multifamily demand in this submarket, or if Prosper's growth trajectory supports both; mixed-use without residential is a red flag for apartment feasibility.

stories.title: Retail Leads as CRE Recovery Diverges Across Sectors, Markets
stories.excerpt: The U.S. commercial real estate recovery is following markedly different paths across property sectors and markets, Integra Realty Resources (IRR) said in its newly released 2026 Mid-Year Viewpoint Report. More than 90% of retail markets surveyed are in recovery or expansion, while office markets remain evenly divided between recovery and recession. Multifamily performance is shaped largely by local supply cycles, while industrial markets are concentrated primarily in the expansion and hypersupply phases. Across all four sectors, IRR’s data show a continued flight to quality, with modern, well-located and specialized properties outperforming older or commodity-oriented assets. Meanwhile, speculative construction has slowed sharply. “National data provide essential context, but the clearest picture emerges when it is informed by what is happening on the ground,” said IRR CEO Anthony M. Graziano. “Investors cannot assume that modest rate cuts will meaningfully improve transaction economics, particularly while long-term borrowing costs and equity return requirements remain elevated. Through year-end and into 2027, we expect opportunities to remain concentrated in markets and assets where the basis, income growth and local demand support the investment case.” The post Retail Leads as CRE Recovery Diverges Across Sectors, Markets appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: IRR 2026 Mid-Year Report: >90% of retail markets in recovery/expansion; office split evenly recovery/recession.
Multifamily performance driven by local supply cycles; industrial concentrated in expansion and hypersupply phases.
Flight-to-quality and modern/specialized assets outperforming; speculative construction slowed sharply across sectors.
stories.summary: Integra Realty Resources' 2026 Mid-Year Viewpoint Report finds divergent sector recovery: retail leads with over 90% of markets in recovery or expansion, office remains split between recovery and recession, multifamily is shaped by local supply cycles, and industrial is concentrated in expansion and hypersupply. Across all sectors, flight-to-quality persists, with modern, specialized, and well-located properties outperforming commodity assets. Speculative construction has slowed significantly, and elevated long-term borrowing costs and equity return requirements are limiting transaction economics.
stories.impact: Multifamily developers face headwinds from elevated equity return requirements and constrained speculative construction pipeline, but local supply cycles present market-specific entry windows. The flight-to-quality trend underscores imperative for new, modern product in strong-demand submarkets; older stock and commodity assets will face pricing pressure. Industrial hypersupply signals competitive pressure on logistics-anchored mixed-use deals and potential softness in retail-warehouse conversions.

stories.title: Mac Cosmetics’ SoHo Flagship Relocates to 5K SF at 579 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Mac Cosmetics has selected a new foundation in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood. The global makeup brand signed a 5,325-square-foot lease at 579 Broadway between Prince and East Houston streets to host its next flagship location in the trendy shopping corridor, according to an announcement from landlord broker Newmark. The deal represents a relocation of just two blocks from Mac’s current perch alongside Bloomingdale’s at 506 Broadway. The landlord at 579 Broadway, Lord Shivas Properties, was represented by Newmark’s Ariel Schuster, Michael Paster and Logan Ryan. Paster said in a statement that the location, neighbored by brands like jewelry brand Pandora and bohemian clothing store Free People Movement, was a “natural fit for Mac Cosmetics.” The brand plans to occupy approximately 3,825 square feet on the ground floor and 1,500 square feet of lower-level space within the five-story building. The length of Mac’s lease and the asking rent were unclear, but a report from CBRE found retail rents near SoHo’s Prince Street averaged $1,408 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026. Mac will take possession of the storefront in January, according to Newmark. Its current occupant, British fashion retailer AllSaints, will occupy the space through the end of the year. A spokesperson for AllSaints did not immediately respond to a request for comment on its future plans in the neighborhood. Cushman & Wakefield’s Mike O’Neill, Jason Greenstone and Taylor Reynolds negotiated the lease on behalf of Mac Cosmetics. The lease offered Mac the opportunity to secure a highly visible location in the corridor, O’Neill told CO in a statement. “We’re pleased to have helped facilitate a transaction that aligns Mac with a location well positioned to support its long-term retail objectives,” O’Neill said. Lord Shivas Properties also owns the lot’s adjacent storefront at 152 Mercer Street, the site of luxury knitwear brand Extreme Cashmere‘s U.S. flagship. Emily
bullets: Mac Cosmetics relocates SoHo flagship 2 blocks to 5,325 SF at 579 Broadway, Manhattan.
Ground floor 3,825 SF plus 1,500 SF lower-level space; neighbors Pandora, Free People Movement.
Move from 506 Broadway alongside Bloomingdale's; lease terms and rent not disclosed.
stories.summary: Mac Cosmetics has signed a lease for its next SoHo flagship at 579 Broadway (between Prince and East Houston Streets), totaling 5,325 square feet across ground floor (3,825 SF) and lower-level (1,500 SF) space in a five-story building. The move relocates the brand two blocks from its current location at 506 Broadway alongside Bloomingdale's. The relocation places Mac alongside premium retail anchors including Pandora and Free People Movement.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Retail migration within SoHo reflects continued strength in luxury consumer spending and foot traffic in Manhattan's premier shopping corridor, but the 2-block relocation signals retail densification rather than new demand generation. Relevant only if developers are evaluating retail-anchored mixed-use projects in SoHo, where competition from established flagships may compress retail margins.

stories.title: Vintage Phoenix Midrise Office Building Slated for Hotel Rooms
stories.excerpt: The building is nearly a 100 years old, but that isn’t stopping Phoenix developers CivicGroup and Sunflower Development from converting the onetime office tower into hotel rooms. Built in 1928, the Security Building will undergo a $135 million renovation that will include 255 hotel rooms. In addition to the hotel rooms, the redevelopment will include 15,000 square feet of meeting space – including the 5,500-square-foot 1928 ballroom – and other amenities. The investor duo hopes to open five food-and-beverage outlets in the hotel, including multiple bars, a three-meal restaurant, and an upscale eatery. The building is currently owned by Maricopa County and will continue to lease the building to the development team as a hotel for at least 20 years. The Phoenix Business Journal reports the project requires a significant amount of preservation work – including the removal of drywall, carpet, non-historic walls and cubicles. The developers hope to start in the first quarter of 2027 and open in Q4 2028. The post Vintage Phoenix Midrise Office Building Slated for Hotel Rooms appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CivicGroup and Sunflower Development converting 1928 Security Building Phoenix into 255-hotel-room property.
$135M renovation; building currently owned/leased by Maricopa County for 20+ years.
Includes 15,000 SF meeting space, five F&B outlets; Phase 1 starts Q1 2027, opens Q4 2028.
stories.summary: Developers CivicGroup and Sunflower Development are converting the 1928 Security Building, a historic Phoenix office tower, into a 255-room hotel through a $135 million renovation. The project includes 15,000 square feet of meeting space (incorporating a historic 5,500-SF ballroom), five food-and-beverage outlets, and a 20-plus-year lease agreement with current owner Maricopa County. Construction is targeted to begin in Q1 2027 with opening in Q4 2028.
stories.impact: Office-to-hotel conversion in Phoenix's downtown core signals weakness in legacy office demand and highlights adaptive reuse as an alternative to multifamily conversion. The long-term county lease provides stable anchor tenant, reducing execution risk. This signals that Phoenix's downtown office market remains challenged; multifamily developers should assess whether downtown Phoenix still supports new residential or if demand is shifting to suburban, employment-proximate markets (Tempe, Chandler, Scottsdale).

stories.title: Law Firm DLA Piper, Insurance Group Ascot Ink Deals at 1251 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Two office tenants at Mitsui Fudosan America’s 1251 Avenue of the Americas are extending or expanding their footprints, Commercial Observer has learned. Law firm DLA Piper expanded by 41,600 square feet on the entire 29th floor of the Midtown building with an 8.5-year term, bringing the law firm to a total of 210,000 square feet at the property between West 49th and West 50th streets. Meanwhile, insurance company Ascot Group signed a 12-year extension for its 44,100-square-foot offices on the entire 43rd floor, according to sources familiar with the deal. Ascot was previously subleasing the space. Asking rent for Ascot’s space was $150 per square foot, while the asking rent for DLA Piper’s deal was $140 per square foot, according to the source. Newmark‘s David Falk, Pete Shimkin, Eric Cagner and Claire Koeppel are exclusive leasing agents for the 54-story office tower, but declined to comment. CBRE‘s John Nugent and Alexander Golod negotiated on behalf of Ascot, while a separate CBRE team of Mike Wellen and Ken Rapp handled the deal for DLA Piper. CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the DLA Piper deal and declined to comment on Ascot. Other recent deals at 1251 Avenue of the Americas include a 41,600-square-foot lease for alternative investing firm LGT Capital Partners in May and an expansion to 80,200 square feet for Trust Company of the West in November 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: DLA Piper expands 41,600 SF at 1251 Avenue of the Americas to total 210,000 SF, 8.5-year term.
Ascot Group extends 44,100 SF on 43rd floor, 12-year term, at $150/SF asking rent.
DLA Piper at $140/SF; both deals signal institutional tenant stability in Midtown office.
stories.summary: At Mitsui Fudosan America's 1251 Avenue of the Americas (West 49th–50th Streets), law firm DLA Piper expanded by 41,600 square feet (29th floor, entire) on an 8.5-year term, bringing its total footprint to 210,000 square feet. Insurance group Ascot Group extended a 12-year lease for its 44,100-square-foot offices (43rd floor) at $150/SF asking rent after previously subleasing. DLA Piper's expansion was negotiated at $140/SF.
stories.impact: Back-to-back large institutional-tenant expansions and long-term commitments at a trophy Midtown office building demonstrate selective resilience in premium Manhattan office, supporting leasing economics and valuations for Class-A properties. However, the flight-to-quality dynamic suggests older, secondary office assets face continued pressure; multifamily conversion or repositioning of lower-tier office stock in Midtown remains a viable alternative strategy.

stories.title: Value Defines Success for Dining Industry in 2026
stories.excerpt: Value has become a defining theme across the dining industry, yet the definition of value can vary across the sector’s diverse restaurant categories and for individual brands, Placer.ai says in a new white paper. A closer look at chains across the industry suggests that, amid ongoing economic pressure, perceptions of value are evolving. Titled Dining In 2026: All Roads Lead To Value, the white paper says that consumers in 2026 appear to be evaluating value through a broader lens that includes experience, quality, convenience and affordability. While overall dining traffic this year has trailed 2025 in most months, some segments are doing better than others, such as fast casual and fine dining. Fast casual in particular has seen a number of dining chains maintaining positive traffic momentum by pairing everyday value with the benefits of full-service dining, reports Placer.ai. Chipotle, for example, has achieved success by pairing menu novelty with loyalty perks to reinforce a value proposition anchored by quality and experience The post Value Defines Success for Dining Industry in 2026 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Placer.ai: Dining value-perception redefined in 2026 to include experience, quality, convenience, affordability.
Fast casual and fine dining outperforming; fast casual maintains positive traffic via loyalty and novelty.
Overall dining traffic trails 2025 in most months; Chipotle succeeds pairing menu novelty with value.
stories.summary: Placer.ai's white paper 'Dining In 2026: All Roads Lead To Value' finds that consumers are evaluating dining through a broader lens encompassing experience, quality, convenience, and affordability amid ongoing economic pressure. While overall dining traffic has trailed 2025 in most months, fast casual and fine dining are outperforming. Fast-casual chains like Chipotle are maintaining positive traffic momentum by pairing everyday value, menu novelty, and loyalty programs with quality and experience positioning.
stories.impact: Weak relevance to multifamily development. Dining-traffic trends inform retail-tenancy strategy and F&B anchor feasibility in mixed-use projects, but do not directly signal residential demand, job growth, or population migration. Relevant only if evaluating food-hall or restaurant-anchored mixed-use development; consumer pullback in casual dining suggests retail margins are compressed and food-service anchors require strong brand positioning.

stories.title: Cellular Provider InfiniG Secures $5M Seed Funding
stories.excerpt: InfiniG, an enterprise cellular platform for commercial real estate, announced Tuesday that it has raised a $5.2 million seed round. Early-stage venture capital firms J2 Ventures and Stormbreaker Ventures led the round. Los Gatos, Calif.-based InfiniG said it will use the funding to expand its mobile coverage as a service (MCaaS) product rollouts, automate mobile-operator integration, scale its InfiniG Insights, and advance the platform’s automation and physical artificial intelligence. InfiniG’s MCaaS platform enables building owners to deploy neutral-host, multicarrier indoor cellular coverage without the complexity and cost of traditional distributed antenna systems, according to the company. The platform also creates an upgradeable foundation for future 5G services, private wireless networks, physical AI and connected-building applications. “The mobile operators — the AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobiles of the world — have traditionally provided coverage,” said Joel Lindholm, co-founder and CEO at InfiniG. “The processes that have been used for the last 10 to 20 years really require people to come into each building using those processes and their own technologies, and that’s been very limiting. That’s why only the biggest buildings or biggest venues have coverage. That’s also why you see most buildings in the United States do not have coverage, whether they be hospitals or hotels, offices, warehouses or manufacturing floors.” Lindholm’s firm stepped into the gap. “Our solution is focused on being able to cover those thousands of buildings instead of the hundreds of buildings from the legacy model. Fundamentally, we have to look at the world in a new way for the next decade. The 10- to 20-year-old technologies are just no longer satisfactory.” InfiniG uses Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS), a non-carrier spectrum, to provide a single radio infrastructure in a building that is shared equally across all the mobile operators. bullets: InfiniG raises $5.2M seed funding from J2 Ventures and Stormbreaker Ventures.
Mobile coverage-as-a-service platform enables neutral-host, multicarrier indoor 5G without traditional DAS complexity.

stories.summary: InfiniG, a Los Gatos-based enterprise cellular platform, has closed a $5.2 million seed round led by J2 Ventures and Stormbreaker Ventures. The company's mobile-coverage-as-a-service (MCaaS) platform allows building owners to deploy neutral-host, multicarrier indoor cellular coverage without the cost and complexity of traditional distributed antenna systems (DAS), while creating an upgradeable foundation for 5G, private wireless networks, physical AI, and connected-building applications. Funding will accelerate MCaaS rollouts, automate mobile-operator integration, and scale automation and physical AI capabilities.
stories.impact: InfiniG's MCaaS platform reduces capital and operational barriers to on-site cellular and 5G deployment in commercial and multifamily buildings, potentially improving amenity value and tenant retention. For multifamily developers, this signals a market opportunity to differentiate new buildings through seamless indoor coverage without heavy infrastructure; reduces capex relative to traditional DAS and positions buildings for future connectivity-dependent uses. Relevant for Class-A multifamily targeting tech-forward tenants and connected-home features.

stories.title: Samantha Atlas of Ash Staging: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Staging can play a critical role in residential real estate. It helps to bring a model unit to life, and it provides potential renters and buyers with a glimpse of what their future home could look like. Successfully staging requires more than a properly positioned couch and some art on the walls. Enter Ash Staging, a luxury staging and model residence design business that has completed thousands of projects — including commercial and hospitality spaces — over the last 15 years, representing over $50 billion in real estate. Samantha Atlas, senior director of projects at Ash Staging, has been with the firm for nine years. She splits her time between Los Angeles and New York City, and helped to launch the company’s West Coast office. Commercial Observer caught up with Atlas in mid-August to discuss her time with Ash Staging and the value of her work in real estate. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What is the mission of Ash Staging? Samantha Atlas: I’ve been with Ash for a little over nine years now, and really seen it grow. I run the L.A. office, and I joined the company at a time of growth. Since I joined, the story has been, “How do we continue to grow and change the narrative of what staging can be?” Generally speaking, for a long time the idea around staging has been neutrality — nothing with a serious point of view. I came to work at Ash because we sort of eschewed that. We want to imbue personality. We want our clients and our potential buyers of these homes to have an emotional response — it’s what drives us. We believe in the power of paint and will really push our clients to invest outside of the staging into the property to get it sold. bullets: Ash Staging is luxury model-residence design and staging firm; 15-year track record across $50B+ real estate.

stories.summary: Ash Staging is a luxury staging and model-residence design firm that has completed over $50 billion in real estate projects across residential, commercial, and hospitality sectors over 15 years. Samantha Atlas, senior director of projects, has been with the firm for nine years and runs its West Coast office while based between Los Angeles and New York City. The article profiles Atlas and the value of professional staging in residential real estate marketing and unit positioning.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development strategy or market signals. Staging is a back-end execution and marketing tool for lease-up and sales. Relevant only if evaluating model-unit design budgets and pre-opening marketing spend for new multifamily communities; the article provides no data on market trends, demand, or capital availability affecting development feasibility.
